questions: Should the random seed be set globally (random.seed) or should a separate random.Random instance be used to avoid affecting other random calls in the program?
Are the predicates case-sensitive? For example, is 'Has_Uppercase' (different capitalization) considered invalid?
If the same predicate appears multiple times in the input list, after deduplication, does the order of predicates in the output dictionary matter?
Should the function handle a length of zero? The prompt says 'specified length' and tests include zero, but is the behavior defined for zero length beyond the test?
Is the character sampling uniform over the combined set, or should each category (letters, digits, punctuation) have equal probability?
Should the function reset the random seed after execution to its previous state?
Are there any constraints on the length (e.g., maximum length) due to memory or performance?
If predicates list is None instead of an empty list, should it be treated as empty or raise an error?
